newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: BOBSLEIGH-WORLD CHAMPIONSHIP GOLD FOR GOETSCHI.
newsitem.headline: BOBSLEIGH-WORLD CHAMPIONSHIP GOLD FOR GOETSCHI.

text.p: Reto Goetschi used home track to his advantage piloting his Swiss sled to a gold medal in the two-man competition at the world bobsleigh championships on Sunday.

Goetschi and breakman Guido Acklin, bronze medallists at last year's championships, clocked the fastest times in three of four trips down the 1.6 kilometre natural ice track finishing with a four-run combined time of four minutes, 17.59 seconds.
Italy's Guenther Huber and Antonio Tartaglia, fresh from a victory at the European championships last weekend, had held a wafer-thin 0.01 seconds advantage on the Swiss duo after the first run.
But the Italians lost ground in each of the next three rounds and settled for silver, almost a second back, with an aggregate time of 4:18.57
Brian Shimer and Robert Olesen of the United States, sixth after the first run, fought back to take the bronze with 4:18.67.

Pierre Lueders and Dave MacEachern of Canada, last year's silver medallists, tied Goetschi for the top time in the final round but missed out on a return to the podium by 0.06 seconds, finishing fourth in 4:18.73.
Fifth place went to the number one German sled of Sepp Dostthaler and Thomas Platzer in 4:19.07.
